terms.popup: A tax status under Subchapter M of the tax code. A BDC that qualifies pays no corporate tax on income it distributes, which is why nearly all of its NII goes out as dividends.
terms.definition: Tax treatment elected under Subchapter M of the Internal Revenue Code. To keep it the company must meet source-of-income and diversification tests and distribute at least 90% of investment company taxable income each year. Tax on distributed income becomes the shareholders' obligation.

terms.popup: To stay tax-free at the fund level, a BDC must pay out at least 90% of its taxable investment income every year. This is why dividends track NII so closely.
terms.definition: The RIC requirement to distribute at least 90% of the sum of investment company taxable income (ordinary income plus net short-term capital gains over net long-term losses, without the dividends-paid deduction) and net tax-exempt income. Non-cash PIK income counts toward the amount that must be paid out.

terms.popup: After-tax NII per share ÷ dividend per share. Above 1.0× the dividend is earned; below it, the BDC is paying from reserves, gains or capital. MAIN Q2 2026: 1.24× on the regular dividend, 0.90× on the total.
terms.definition: Regular coverage = after-tax NII per share ÷ regular dividend per share; total coverage = ÷ (regular + supplemental + special). BXSL Q2 2026: $0.75 vs $0.77 = 0.97×. Rule: regular coverage under 1.0× for two consecutive quarters is a flag; a special dividend with total coverage under 1.0× is a note.
terms.source: This site's own ratio on the tagged 10-Q facts (BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 for the Q2 2026 figures)

terms.term: regular vs supplemental vs special dividend
terms.popup: Regular is the base quarterly payout the board intends to keep. Supplemental is an extra tied to excess income; special is a one-off, often from gains or spillover. Coverage is read against each.
terms.definition: Split from the 10-Q dividend note; where the note does not split, the site labels the amount 'total'. Dividends per share come from InvestmentCompanyDistributionToShareholdersPerShare (YTD, differenced), with the site's fixed fallback order. Distributions are at the board's discretion and depend on earnings and RIC status.

terms.popup: The return a shareholder earned on book value: change in NAV per share plus dividends, divided by starting NAV. BXSL: 1.2% for the first half of 2026. Shown YTD or trailing four quarters, never as one quarter unless tagged.
terms.definition: BXSL's definition: 'the change in NAV per share during the period, plus distributions per share (assuming dividends and distributions are reinvested ...) divided by the beginning NAV per share.' XBRL InvestmentCompanyTotalReturn is year-to-date for most filers (three-month for 7 of 50), so the site derives (NAV_t − NAV_t−1 + distributions) ÷ NAV_t−1 over the same span when needed.

terms.term: net increase in net assets from operations
terms.popup: A BDC's bottom line: NII plus realized and unrealized gains and losses. It moves with the marks, so it is noisier than NII and is never used to derive the fourth quarter.
terms.definition: The GAAP net income of an investment company (XBRL NetIncomeLoss): net investment income + net realized gains (losses) + net change in unrealized appreciation (depreciation). BXSL Q2 2026: $9.5M against NII of $173.8M, the gap being marks. Gains where not tagged = this line − after-tax NII.
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.2 Realized and unrealized gains row and closing note

terms.popup: Realized: the profit or loss locked in when a loan is repaid, sold or written off. Unrealized: the change in the marks on loans still held. Both sit below NII and drive NAV.
terms.definition: Realized gains are the difference between net proceeds and amortized cost using specific identification, including charge-offs net of recoveries. Unrealized appreciation or depreciation is the period change in fair value versus cost on holdings still owned. XBRL RealizedInvestmentGainsLosses and UnrealizedGainLossOnInvestments where tagged (OBDC tags both), else NetIncomeLoss − after-tax NII.
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.2 Realized and unrealized gains row

terms.popup: The manager's fair value on a loan relative to what it cost. Below 1.0 the book is carrying an unrealized loss; a mark well under cost before a loan stops paying is the early warning.
terms.definition: Portfolio mark = Σ InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue ÷ Σ InvestmentOwnedAtCost. ARCC 0.995, BXSL 0.964, FSK 0.906, MAIN 1.157 (equity-heavy). Loans are marked under ASC 820 and Rule 2a-5, mostly as Level 3 (unobservable inputs), by or under the direction of the board.

terms.popup: Fair value divided by amortized cost. ARCC 0.989 and BXSL 0.964 at Jun 30 2026; MAIN 1.155 because of its equity positions.
terms.definition: Per holding: InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue ÷ InvestmentOwnedAtCost from the schedule of investments. Equity positions and warrants lift the portfolio ratio (MAIN, HTGC run above 1.0), so the distressed share is computed on third-party debt only.
terms.source: This site's own ratio: InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue ÷ InvestmentOwnedAtCost per holding from the schedule of investments, and in total from SEC EDGAR companyfacts
terms.whereUsed: Holdings table L8; watchlist L9; chart L7
terms.fixNote: popup replaced per the refuter

terms.popup: What the BDC paid for a loan, adjusted over time for any discount or fees it accretes into income. It is the 'cost' side of every mark and yield calculation.
terms.definition: Purchase price plus accreted original issue discount and minus amortized premium and capitalized fees to date; realized gains are measured against it. The schedule's cost column (the data set's 'Adjusted cost basis') and the tag InvestmentOwnedAtCost carry it. Weighted-average yield at cost divides by it.

terms.popup: The price a loan would fetch in an orderly sale today, as estimated by the BDC's board and valuation firms. Most private loans have no quote, so fair value is a model, not a trade.
terms.definition: ASC 820: 'the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the applicable measurement date'; Rule 2a-5 governs values where market quotations are not readily available. Tagged as InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue; the portfolio total is the size measure for the universe ranking.
terms.whereUsed: Portfolio size; mark; every FV-based ratio

terms.popup: A loan the BDC has stopped booking interest on because it doubts it will be paid in full. The closest thing private credit has to a default rate. BXSL: 3.6% of cost, 1.8% of fair value at June 30, 2026.
terms.definition: Loans are placed on non-accrual 'when there is reasonable doubt whether principal or interest will be collected in full'; accrued interest is reversed and OID stops accreting. Non-accrual rate = cost (or fair value) of non-accrual investments ÷ total investments at cost (fair value); a second line over debt investments only. Read from the schedule footnote ('(17) Loan was on non-accrual status'), which only GBDC tags in XBRL.
terms.whereUsed: Scorecard; chart L7; watchlist L9; composite

terms.popup: Interest paid by adding to the loan balance instead of in cash. The BDC books it as income now and collects it at maturity, if at all. A rising PIK share with flat NII means cash earnings are falling.
terms.definition: 'PIK represents interest that is accrued and recorded as interest income at the contractual rates, increases the loan principal on the respective capitalization dates, and is generally due at maturity.' It must still be distributed under the RIC rules even though no cash has arrived. Two ratios on the site: PIK income ÷ total investment income, and PIK interest ÷ (cash + PIK interest). BXSL Q2 2026: 6.6%; ARCC 15.8% of total investment income.
terms.workingRef: blueprint §3.3 PIK share row, §8 PIK share
terms.whereUsed: Scorecard; chart L7; holdings PIK flag

terms.popup: A loan feature that lets the borrower pay some or all interest in more debt. Shown on a holding as 'SOFR + 5.25% (incl. 2.88% PIK)'. Fine when agreed at signing; a warning when added later.
terms.definition: The per-loan PIK rate is tagged as InvestmentInterestRatePaidInKind (179 facts on BXSL's instance) and printed in the schedule's rate column. If the company expects the PIK will not be realized, the loan goes on non-accrual and the uncapitalized accrual is reversed.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30; the BXSL 10-Q XBRL instance (accession 0001736035-26-000016)

terms.popup: Contractual PIK was in the loan from day one, a feature of the deal. Amended PIK was switched on later to relieve a struggling borrower, a symptom. Filings rarely say which, so the site shows the total.
terms.definition: The caveat on every PIK figure: the same ratio can mean a portfolio built around PIK-toggle structures or a book where borrowers have stopped paying cash. In the two-track frame, PIK conversions and amendments are the private analogue of distressed exchanges and are read beside non-accruals, never summed with them.
terms.source: The BDC's own 10-Q PIK disclosure; PitchBook 2023 Annual Global Private Debt Report for the two-track default frame; this site's reading note

terms.term: weighted-average yield at cost and at fair value
terms.popup: The average interest rate the debt book earns, weighted by each loan's size. At cost it is what the BDC paid for; at fair value it is what today's marks imply. BXSL: 9.2% at cost, 9.4% at fair value.
terms.definition: BXSL's footnote: '(a) the annual stated interest rate or yield plus the annual accretion of discounts or less the annual amortization of premiums ... on accruing debt ... divided by (b) total debt investments (at fair value or amortized cost, as applicable)'. Site formula: Σ(principal × all-in rate) over accruing debt ÷ Σ amortized cost (or fair value) of the same holdings, computed before discount accretion and so 0-0.3 points under the filer's figure. Excludes non-accruals.
terms.whereUsed: Scorecard; composite strip; net interest margin

terms.popup: When a loan is issued below par, the discount is booked into income a little each period until maturity. It lifts reported yield without any cash arriving and stops when a loan goes on non-accrual.
terms.definition: Original issue discount and market discount are accreted to interest income over the life of the loan; accretion ceases on the date a loan is placed on non-accrual. Not tagged per loan, so the site's computed yield is labeled 'before discount accretion'. The filer's own yield includes it.

terms.popup: The part of the debt book whose interest resets with a base rate like SOFR. Near 100% for most BDCs (BXSL 99.3%), so falling rates cut income unless floors bite.
terms.definition: Cost of holdings carrying a spread fact ÷ cost of debt holdings, cross-checked against the filing's own sentence ('99.3% of our performing debt investments based on fair value ... were at floating rates'). Links the SOFR tile to the interest-rate sensitivity table.

terms.popup: Golub's name for its unitranche: a single senior secured loan covering the whole debt need. GBDC's book is 87% one stop at cost, which the site counts as first lien.
terms.definition: A filer-specific label. GBDC: one stop $7,288.8M of $8,377.1M at cost = 87.0%, senior secured 4.7%, so first lien including one stop is about 92%. Mapped to the first-lien class with the raw label kept on every holding.
terms.source: GBDC's schedule of investments (the 'one stop' label and its totals at cost); this site's lien-mix mapping

terms.popup: A slice of a first-lien loan that agrees to be repaid after the 'first-out' slice. Same collateral, lower place in the queue, higher rate. The site keeps it in first lien but labels it.
terms.definition: A tranche created by an agreement among lenders inside a first-lien or unitranche facility that sets a payment waterfall between first-out and last-out holders. Classified as 'first lien incl. unitranche/last-out', never second lien, with the raw label preserved.
terms.source: BDC schedules of investments, where the tranche is labeled 'first lien, last-out'; this site's lien-mix labels

terms.popup: Debt that ranks below the secured lenders and is paid only after them. Mezzanine is the classic form, often with warrants attached. It behaves more like equity when a borrower struggles.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'Mezzanine: Subordinated debt, generally with features similar to preferred equity, such as warrants. Often used in LBO transactions.' Grouped with unsecured in the lien mix; included in LCD's BDC all-in yield series ('senior secured, unsecured & subordinated debt holdings').
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report; LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slide 33 source line

terms.popup: Holdings that are securities of a structure rather than loans to a company: CLO equity, joint-venture certificates, asset-backed notes. Grouped as 'vehicles' and kept out of the loan statistics.
terms.definition: Lien-mix class for CLO and JV certificates and similar paper, routed to the vehicles class. LCD's maturity wall likewise 'Excludes equity, CMBS and CLO holdings'.
terms.source: LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slide 31 source line

terms.popup: Capital a BDC puts to work through a structure it owns or co-owns (a joint venture, loan program, asset manager, CLO equity, REIT) instead of a direct loan. Yield there comes partly from leverage inside the vehicle.
terms.definition: Holdings typed JV, SLP, asset manager, CLO equity or REIT, shown as a share-of-fair-value tile. ARCC: 15.3% controlled, with Ivy Hill Asset Management 9.7% of fair value at a 17.9% yield on cost and SDLP certificates 4% at 13.2%. Top-10 concentration, yield, first-lien share, the spread histogram and the distressed share are computed on third-party debt only.
terms.source: ARCC 10-Q 2026-06-30 (the financial report's R2.htm and R4.htm; the Ivy Hill and SDLP disclosures); this site's own vehicle typing

terms.popup: A lending partnership the BDC co-owns with another investor. The BDC books its share as one investment, and the venture borrows on its own, so its yield is levered.
terms.definition: A controlled or affiliated entity, usually formed with an insurer or pension, that originates or holds loans with its own financing. Reported as a single large holding (and often as a fair-value-only subtotal in the data set), it belongs to the vehicles class.
terms.source: ARCC 10-Q 2026-06-30 (the SDLP disclosure); SEC BDC data set, July 2026 soi.tsv (joint-venture subtotal rows)

terms.popup: ARCC's joint venture that holds first-lien loans and funds them with its own debt; ARCC holds subordinated certificates yielding 13.2%. A vehicle, not a loan.
terms.definition: The Senior Direct Lending Program (SDLP): ARCC's certificates were 4% of fair value with a 13.2% yield on cost at June 30, 2026, and the program appears in the data set as a fair-value-only subtotal of $1,153.7M. Classified as a vehicle.
terms.source: ARCC 10-Q 2026-06-30 (the yield table and the SDLP disclosure); SEC BDC data set, July 2026 soi.tsv (the SDLP fair-value subtotal row)

terms.popup: A portfolio company the BDC controls, presumed when it owns more than 25% of the voting stock. Income and marks are reported separately for these, and the site keeps them out of the loan statistics.
terms.definition: 1940 Act §2(a)(9): control is 'the power to exercise a controlling influence over the management or policies', presumed above 25% of voting securities. BXSL: 'deemed to "control" a portfolio company if the Company owns more than 25% of its outstanding voting securities and/or held the power to exercise control'. Affiliation comes from InvestmentIssuerAffiliationAxis (member text '| affiliation').
terms.source: 15 U.S.C. §80a-2(a)(9) (law.cornell.edu); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30

terms.popup: A portfolio company in which the BDC owns 5% to 25% of the voting stock: enough to be an 'affiliated person' under the 1940 Act, not enough to control it.
terms.definition: 1940 Act §2(a)(3): an affiliated person includes any owner of 5% or more of voting securities. BXSL: 'deemed an "affiliated person" of a portfolio company if the Company owns 5% or more of the portfolio company's outstanding voting securities'. The three classes on the site are non-controlled/non-affiliated, non-controlled affiliated and controlled.
terms.source: 15 U.S.C. §80a-2(a)(3) (law.cornell.edu); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30

terms.popup: A business the BDC has lent to or invested in. The count is a diversification measure: BXSL had 313 at June 30, 2026.
terms.definition: Distinct issuer members on the typed InvestmentIdentifierAxis, third-party only, cross-checked against the filing's own count ('Number of portfolio companies 313'). Under the 1940 Act a BDC cannot hold more than 25% of assets in a single investment.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30; MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets

terms.popup: The share of the portfolio in the ten largest borrowers. Higher means one bad loan hurts more. Computed on third-party debt so a joint venture does not dominate the list.
terms.definition: Σ fair value of the ten largest third-party issuers ÷ portfolio fair value, from the schedule of investments. Vehicles and summary members ('Largest Portfolio Company Investment', 'Top Five ...') are excluded before ranking.
terms.source: This site's own ratio on the parsed schedule of investments (the ten largest issuers ÷ total fair value)

terms.popup: The portfolio split by borrower industry, top ten. Commercial services and software dominate BDC books (21.2% and 17.9% of holdings by count, LCD Q2 2026). Read point changes with a small-base caveat.
terms.definition: EquitySecuritiesByIndustryAxis facts or the schedule's industry section headers. Composite and per-BDC bars on chart L6; LCD's slide 30 gives the industry benchmark by count.
terms.source: LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slide 30; the same deck, chart 24 series 2Q26 (Commercial Services 0.2117, Software 0.1787)

terms.popup: When the BDC's borrowers must repay or refinance, stacked by year. A heavy near-term share in a tight market means extensions and amendments ahead. LCD: the largest BDC share falls in 2031-2033.
terms.definition: Σ cost of third-party debt by maturity year in LCD's buckets (2026 ... 2030, 2031-2033, later), from the HTML schedule's Maturity Date column; revolvers and delayed-draw loans by their own maturity with unfunded balances shown separately; equity, CLO, CMBS and vehicles excluded, as LCD does.
terms.source: LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slides 31-32
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.2 Maturity wall row, §4.3 chart L5, §7.3, §8

terms.popup: A term loan the borrower can draw in pieces up to a deadline, usually to fund acquisitions. Until drawn it is an unfunded commitment that earns no interest.
terms.definition: Listed in the commitments table by type ('Delayed Draw Term Loan') with a commitment expiration date and unfunded amount. 'Position or portion thereof is an unfunded commitment, and no interest is being earned on the unfunded portion, although the investment may be subject to unused commitment fees.'

terms.popup: A credit line that can be drawn, repaid and redrawn. On the asset side it is a commitment to a borrower; on the liability side it is the BDC's own bank line, whose undrawn room is its liquidity.
terms.definition: Asset side: 'Revolver' rows in the unfunded-commitment table. Liability side: the BDC's Revolving Credit Facility, with covenants such as 'maintain at all times a 150% asset coverage ratio'; undrawn capacity is tagged LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity (BXSL $2.63B).

terms.popup: Money the BDC has promised to lend but has not yet handed over, mostly on revolvers and delayed-draw loans. It must be fundable from cash and undrawn lines, and it counts when planning leverage.
terms.definition: Σ InvestmentCompanyFinancialCommitmentToInvesteeFutureAmount per holding (714 facts on BXSL's instance; 1,093 dimensioned rows in the July data set). The dimensionless companyfacts value must be reconciled per filer (ARCC's $33M is one member; PFLT's $603.6M is the total). BXSL: 'we maintain sufficient borrowing capacity within the 150% asset coverage limitation to cover any outstanding unfunded commitments'.

terms.popup: (Cash + undrawn revolver) ÷ unfunded commitments. Above 1.0× the BDC can fund everything it has promised without raising money.
terms.definition: Derived weekly from cash, LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity (or the liquidity paragraph) and the reconciled unfunded-commitment total.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity; the BDC's 10-Q liquidity paragraph; this site's own ratio

terms.popup: How the BDC itself is funded: unsecured notes versus secured lines (SPVs, CLOs, revolver), what falls due in the next year, and the undrawn revolver.
terms.definition: Unsecured vs secured share of debt from DebtInstrumentAxis members (BXSL carries 303 such facts); next-12-month maturities from LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths; undrawn revolver; the manager's stated target leverage. BXSL's debt 'consisted of asset based leverage facilities, a revolving credit facility, unsecured note issuances and debt securitizations'.

terms.popup: A wholly owned subsidiary that holds a slice of the loans and borrows against them from a bank. The lender can only look to the SPV's assets, not the whole BDC.
terms.definition: BXSL's SPV Financing Facilities (Jackson Hole Funding, Breckenridge Funding, Big Sky Funding, BXSL CLO 2025-1): secured by 'a first priority security interest in all of the applicable SPV's portfolio investments and cash' and 'non-recourse to the Company'. Counted as secured debt in the liability ladder and inside the consolidated asset-coverage test.

terms.popup: The BDC packages its own loans into a securitization and sells rated notes against them, keeping the equity. Cheap, long-dated, secured funding that still counts toward asset coverage.
terms.definition: 'Term debt securitizations are also known as collateralized loan obligations and are a form of secured financing incurred by the Company, which is consolidated ... and subject to its overall asset coverage requirement.' BXSL's 2024-1 Debt Securitization was $746.8M. LCD tracks US private credit/middle-market CLO issuance separately (deck slide 37).
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30; LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slide 37
terms.whereUsed: Liability ladder; market view CLO chart

terms.popup: Bonds the BDC issues with no specific collateral. Their indentures usually require the BDC to keep meeting the 1940 Act asset-coverage test, so the statutory ratio is also a bond covenant.
terms.definition: BXSL's Unsecured Notes contain 'covenants requiring the Company to comply with the asset coverage requirements of Section 18(a)(1)(A) as modified by Section 61(a)(1) and (2) of the 1940 Act, whether or not it is subject to those requirements'. Their share of total debt is the unsecured share in the liability ladder.

terms.popup: The debt-to-equity range the manager says it aims to run at, stated in the 10-Q. Compare with actual gross and net debt-to-equity and with the statutory cushion.
terms.definition: Read from the 10-Q liquidity discussion with the sentence as provenance and stored with the liability ladder; not computed.
terms.source: The BDC's own stated target debt-to-equity range, from its 10-Q or earnings release; this site's disclosed-only rule

terms.popup: Gross: total debt ÷ net assets. Net: (debt − cash) ÷ net assets. A 150% asset-coverage BDC can run to about 2.0× gross; most sit near 1.0-1.2×.
terms.definition: Debt from the first available of DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount, LongTermDebt, DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount, LinesOfCreditCurrent, else the sum of DebtInstrumentAxis members; never the dimensionless LineOfCredit alone. Sanity check 0.5 × Liabilities ≤ debt ≤ Liabilities. Shown on the secondary axis of chart L3.
terms.source: SEC EDGAR companyfacts for ARCC, BXSL, MAIN, OBDC, FSK and GBDC (checked 2026-09-10)
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.2 Debt and Debt-to-equity rows, §4.3 chart L3

terms.popup: How much NII moves if base rates shift 100 bps, from the filer's own Item 3 table. BXSL: +$132.6M income, −$23.8M expense, +$108.8M net per year for a 100 bp rise.
terms.definition: 'Interest rate sensitivity refers to the change in earnings that may result from changes in the level of interest rates.' Every BDC 10-Q carries an 'Up/Down 100 basis points' table considering floors and ceilings; the site parses interest income, interest expense and net with the sentence as provenance. It links the SOFR tile to NII per share.

terms.popup: The base fee an external manager charges on the BDC's assets, paid whether or not the fund makes money. BXSL: 1.0% a year of gross assets, $35.3M in Q2 2026.
terms.definition: 'payable quarterly in arrears at an annual rate of 1.0% of the average value of the Company's "gross assets" ... excluding undrawn commitments but including assets purchased with borrowed amounts.' XBRL ManagementFeeExpense (42 of 50); blank and labeled 'internally managed' for MAIN, HTGC, TRIN and CSWC, never 0%. Because it is charged on gross (levered) assets, it is not comparable with a fund's 2% on committed capital.

terms.popup: The manager's share of NII above a hurdle (BXSL: 17.5%; the fee card records each filer's rate). It is charged on accrued income, including PIK not yet received, and can be paid even when NAV is falling unless a cap or lookback applies.
terms.definition: BXSL: 17.5% of Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income Returns above a 1.5% quarterly hurdle with 100% catch-up, measured over trailing twelve quarters and subject to an Incentive Fee Cap. 'Shareholders may be charged a fee on an income amount that is higher than the income they may ultimately receive.' XBRL IncentiveFeeExpenseIncomeBased (12 of 50) or IncentiveFeeExpense (19); a quarter with no fact is left empty, never zero.
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.2 Incentive fee row, §4.3 fee card
terms.fixNote: PR B: popup edited (The manager's share of NII above a hurdl...)

terms.popup: The minimum return on net assets the BDC must earn before the manager gets an incentive fee. BXSL: 1.5% a quarter (6.0% a year).
terms.definition: 'Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income Returns, expressed as a rate of return on the value of the Company's net assets at the end of the immediately preceding quarter, is compared to a "hurdle rate" of return of 1.5% per quarter (6.0% annualized).' The hurdle amount is 1.5% × NAV at the start of each quarter in the lookback window.

terms.popup: Once income clears the hurdle, the manager takes 100% of the next slice until it has received its full percentage of everything. BXSL's catch-up runs from 1.5% to 1.82% a quarter.
terms.definition: 'The Adviser will be paid 100% of the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income Returns ... that exceeds the hurdle amount ... but is less than or equal to ... the "Catch-up Amount," determined as the sum of 1.82% (7.27% annualized), multiplied by the Company's NAV'; above that, 17.5%. The effect is that the hurdle protects shareholders only when income is near it.

terms.popup: A fee test over several quarters (BXSL: twelve) that reduces the income fee if the BDC has taken capital losses. Without it, the manager can collect income fees while NAV falls.
terms.definition: BXSL's Incentive Fee Cap: 17.5% of Cumulative Net Return over the Trailing Twelve Quarters minus fees already paid, where Cumulative Net Return is pre-incentive-fee NII minus any Net Capital Loss over the same window. If the cap is zero or negative no income fee is paid. The site's governance flag: income fees that keep accruing while NAV falls, unless a lookback or cap applies.

terms.popup: The manager's share of realized gains, net of all realized and unrealized losses, settled once a year. It is accrued as marks move and reversed when they fall, so it is shown apart from the cash fee load.
terms.definition: BXSL: 17.5% of realized capital gains on a cumulative basis from inception, 'computed net of all realized capital losses and unrealized capital depreciation', less amounts previously paid. XBRL IncentiveFeeExpenseCapitalGainBased or the statement line (ARCC −$21M in Q2 2026).

terms.popup: Annualized running costs excluding interest, as a share of average net assets: 4 × (total expenses − interest) ÷ average net assets. The one cost measure that compares internal and external managers.
terms.definition: Cross-checked against the tagged InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioIncludingIncentiveFee (ARCC 10.89% H1 2026 annualized, FSK 13.18%, HTGC 9.88%, OBDC 12.9%) or ...BeforeIncentiveAllocation (PSEC 10.55%, TSLX 14.11%) minus the interest ratio. Compared with the peer median and the fee card, never with 2/20.
terms.source: us-gaap investment-company taxonomy elements InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioIncludingIncentiveFee and InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioBeforeIncentiveAllocation on SEC EDGAR companyfacts; this site's own ratio

terms.popup: The BDC employs its own staff and pays salaries instead of paying an outside adviser. No management or incentive fee line: MAIN, HTGC, TRIN and CSWC.
terms.definition: A BDC without an external investment adviser. Its costs appear as compensation and general expenses, so the management-fee cell is blank and labeled 'internally managed', never 0%, and the operating expense ratio is the comparable measure.
terms.source: The BDC's own 10-K description of its management structure; this site's fee card

terms.popup: The BDC has no employees; an affiliated adviser runs it for a management fee plus incentive fees under an advisory agreement. Most listed BDCs, including ARCC and BXSL.
terms.definition: BXSL: 'structured as an externally managed, non-diversified, closed-end management investment company'; it 'pays the Adviser a fee for its services under the Investment Advisory Agreement consisting of two components: a management fee and an incentive fee'. The site reads each fee schedule from the 10-K's advisory-agreement note.
terms.workingRef: blueprint §4.3 fee schedule card; fee schedule stored in terms.json
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (BXSL: 'structured as an externally manag...)

terms.popup: The XBRL family InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatio..., which filers tag inconsistently (year-to-date, with or without incentive fees, sometimes annualized). The site uses them only as a cross-check.
terms.definition: InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioIncludingIncentiveFee, InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioBeforeIncentiveAllocation and relatives; InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatio itself is tagged by no listed filer. Three-month coverage in frames CY2026Q2 is 1 of 50; the ratio InvestmentCompanyInvestmentIncomeLossRatio is annualized by BXSL but not by MAIN, so it is never used for NII return on NAV.
terms.source: us-gaap investment-company taxonomy elements InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioIncludingIncentiveFee, InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatioBeforeIncentiveAllocation and InvestmentCompanyExpenseRatio; SEC XBRL frames, CY2026Q2, for the coverage counts

terms.popup: The loan-by-loan table in every BDC 10-Q and 10-K: borrower, lien type, spread, rate, maturity, principal, cost, fair value and footnotes such as non-accrual. It is the raw material of the holdings table.
terms.definition: HTML columns: Spread, Interest Rate, Acquisition Date, Maturity Date, Par Amount/Units, Cost, Fair Value, % of Net Assets; section headers by lien type and industry; footnotes flag non-accrual, unfunded and affiliation. The same facts are tagged per holding on InvestmentIdentifierAxis and republished by the SEC in soi.tsv.
terms.source: The BXSL 10-Q XBRL instance (accession 0001736035-26-000016) and its HTML schedule of investments table
terms.whereUsed: Holdings table L8; every schedule-based metric

terms.popup: The machine-readable tags embedded in SEC filings since 2009. Each number in a 10-Q carries a standard name (a tag), a period and units, which is what lets the site read 50 BDCs automatically.
terms.definition: 'XBRL, in a separate XML file or more recently embedded in quarterly and annual HTML reports as inline XBRL, was first required by the SEC in 2009. XBRL facts must be associated for a standard US-GAAP or IFRS taxonomy.' The site reads companyfacts, frames, the BDC data set and, for the current month, the inline instance.
terms.source: SEC EDGAR APIs page (sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces, fetched 2026-09-11)

terms.popup: The SEC API that returns every tagged fact one company has ever filed, in one JSON file (data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK##########.json). The site's per-BDC history comes from it.
terms.definition: 'This API returns all the company concepts data for a company into a single API call.' Facts are dimensionless (entity-wide), so per-loan values are not in it. The latest quarter can lag frames or the instance, so the site reconciles before calling a period latest.
terms.source: SEC EDGAR APIs page (sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces)

terms.popup: The SEC API that returns one fact per filer for one tag and one calendar period (e.g. NetAssetValuePerShare for CY2026Q2I). It is how the site finds all 50 BDCs at once and counts who tags what.
terms.definition: 'The xbrl/frames API aggregates one fact for each reporting entity that is last filed that most closely fits the calendrical period requested', for annual, quarterly and instantaneous data. Because it snaps to calendar quarters, non-calendar filers (SAR's May 31 instant lands in CY2026Q2I) and fiscal-year-end quarters (PSEC) need the companyfacts or derived fallback.
terms.source: SEC EDGAR APIs page (sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces)

terms.popup: An XBRL dimension value the filer types in as free text, such as 'Issuer name N | affiliation', instead of picking from a fixed list. Each loan in a BDC schedule is one typed member.
terms.definition: SEC BDC data set readme: 'For typed dimensions, the member is a user-supplied string with an empty version, indicated by empty parentheses (e.g., InvestmentIdentifierAxis (us-gaap/2025)=Senior Secured Loan | XYZ Corp()).' Explicit members, by contrast, are taxonomy tags such as InvestmentUnaffiliatedIssuerMember.
terms.source: SEC BDC data set readme.htm (2026_07_bdc.zip, sec.gov), NUM table segments field; the BXSL 10-Q XBRL instance (InvestmentIdentifierAxis typed members)

terms.popup: The XBRL axis that names each individual holding. Facts hanging off it (cost, fair value, spread, rate, principal, unfunded amount) give loan-level detail for every BDC.
terms.definition: us-gaap:InvestmentIdentifierAxis, a typed dimension. On BXSL's 2026-06-30 instance: 1,285 investment members, each carrying InvestmentOwnedAtCost, InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue, InvestmentOwnedPercentOfNetAssets, InvestmentBasisSpreadVariableRate, InvestmentInterestRate, InvestmentOwnedBalancePrincipalAmount, InvestmentCompanyFinancialCommitmentToInvesteeFutureAmount and, where relevant, PIK rate and floor. Portfolio-company count = distinct third-party members.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy axis InvestmentIdentifierAxis; the BXSL 10-Q XBRL instance (accession 0001736035-26-000016)
terms.whereUsed: Holdings table; unfunded commitments; portfolio-company count

terms.popup: The SEC's monthly zip of every BDC's tagged financial statements and schedule of investments, flattened into tab-separated tables. One download covers every loan of every BDC that filed that month.
terms.definition: 'The data set provides information extracted from eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) submissions filed with the Commission in a flattened data format ... submitted by business development companies.' Scope: submissions with an 814- file number or an N-54A filer. Members: datasets/sub, tag, num, txt, pre, cal, non .tsv and soi.tsv at the root; published at sec.gov/files/datastandardsinnovation/data/business-development-company-bdc-data-sets/YYYY_MM_bdc.zip, about ten days after month end.
terms.source: SEC BDC data set readme.htm (2026_07_bdc.zip, sec.gov)

terms.popup: The schedule-of-investments table inside the SEC BDC data set: one row per holding per filing, with cost, fair value, principal, spread, rate, PIK rate and floor already pivoted into columns.
terms.definition: 'SOI - schedule of investments; provides a pivoted report to create a version of the schedule of investments from the tagged data from each BDC financial statement filing.' 60 columns; cost and fair value sit in 'Adjusted cost basis' and 'Initial fair value of Investment'. Rows are kept when the identifier is non-empty, ddate equals period, and both cost and fair value are present; Σ cost and Σ FV must reconcile to the entity totals within 0.5%.
terms.source: SEC BDC data set readme.htm (2026_07_bdc.zip, sec.gov), column names and the row rule

terms.popup: The earnings release a company attaches to its 8-K. For BDCs it often carries figures the 10-Q lacks, such as core NII and borrower leverage; yields on new loans appear in either.
terms.definition: Form 8-K Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) is triggered by public disclosure of material information about a completed quarter; the release is furnished as an exhibit under Item 9.01. The site parses the sentence and stores it as provenance; nothing from it is computed.
terms.source: SEC Form 8-K instructions (sec.gov/files/form8-k.pdf), Items 2.02 and 9.01
terms.fixNote: popup replaced per the refuter

terms.popup: The quarterly report. For a BDC it holds the balance sheet, income statement, schedule of investments, fee and tax notes, the asset-coverage sentence and the rate-sensitivity table.
terms.definition: Filed three times a year (the fourth quarter is in the 10-K). Its XBRL facts populate companyfacts and frames; the inline instance is read directly for filings from the current month. Many income facts are tagged year-to-date, hence the differencing rule.
terms.source: SEC Form 10-Q general instructions (sec.gov); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30; this site's differencing rule

terms.popup: The annual report. It carries the full-year figures, the tax note with spillover, the advisory-agreement note with the fee schedule, and whether the BDC elected 150% coverage.
terms.definition: The site derives the fourth fiscal quarter as the 10-K minus the filer's own three 10-Qs, keyed on NII, never on NetIncomeLoss. The fee card and sbaExempt are parsed from the 10-K with the accession as provenance.
terms.source: SEC Form 10-K general instructions (sec.gov); the BDC's 10-K advisory-agreement note; this site's derived-Q4 rule

terms.popup: The month a filer closes its books. Nine of the 50 BDCs are not December filers (GBDC, OCSL, PFLT, PNNT, GLAD Sept 30; CSWC, GAIN Mar 31; PSEC Jun 30; SAR Feb 28), so their quarters do not line up with calendar frames.
terms.definition: Read from fiscalYearEnd in the submissions JSON and passed explicitly as fyEndMonth to the series builders. Series are labeled by calendar period-end date, never by fiscal quarter number.
terms.source: SEC EDGAR submissions JSON (data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json), fiscalYearEnd field, checked 2026-09-10

terms.popup: A tagged number that covers the fiscal year so far, not one quarter. Most BDCs tag total return, NII per share, distributions and PIK this way, so the site subtracts the prior YTD to get the quarter.
terms.definition: Read the fact's start date first. Where a three-month fact exists the site uses it (HTGC, MSDL, CSWC and GBDC tag distributions that way); otherwise it subtracts the prior year-to-date figure from the current one, within the same fiscal year only. Three-month coverage in frames CY2026Q2: 7 of 50 for total return, 18 for NII per share, 7 for distributions.
terms.source: SEC XBRL frames, CY2026Q2, for the three-month coverage counts; this site's own year-to-date fill rule
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Read the fact's start date first. Where ...)

terms.popup: Turning a year-to-date figure into a single quarter by subtracting the previous year-to-date figure. Only done inside one fiscal year and only when the earlier quarters exist.
terms.definition: Applied to YTD income facts and to derive the fourth quarter (year minus the first three quarters). Balance-sheet figures need no arithmetic. Nothing is derived from a gap and nothing already reported is overwritten.
terms.source: This site's own construction: the derived fourth quarter and the year-to-date fill, applied inside one fiscal year only
terms.workingRef: scripts/lib/statements.mjs (the derived-Q4 and year-to-date fill comments)
terms.fixNote: PR B: source edited (This site's own construction: the derive...)

terms.popup: The site's own private credit index: the top 30 BDCs aggregated, weighted by the cost of their third-party loans, with n stated on every figure.
terms.definition: Computed at refresh time and stored once: all-in yield, spread over base, total-investment-income yield on average cost, spread histogram, maturity wall, sector and lien mix, floating and vehicle share, non-accrual, PIK, FV/cost, distressed share, leverage, asset coverage, operating expense ratio, plus dispersion. The stored file carries the site's credit-data version stamp.
terms.source: This site's own method for the Lenders view composite
terms.whereUsed: Chart L10 strip; every 'vs composite' comparison
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Computed at refresh time and stored once...)

terms.popup: The spread of a metric across the 30 BDCs: min, P25, median, P75, max. It shows where one BDC sits in the pack, which matters more than the number alone.
terms.definition: Stored per ratio in the composite; the P25 of price/NAV feeds the severity stripe. Drawn as chart L11, one row per metric, 30 dots on a shared scale, the selected BDC in accent, the composite median as a tick.
terms.source: This site's own method for the Lenders view composite

terms.popup: The eight BDCs closest to the one selected, by portfolio size, first-lien share and non-accrual rate. Drawn only from the 50 listed BDCs, never from operating companies.
terms.definition: This site's own peer rule for BDCs. From a pool of at least six other BDCs it keeps the eight closest, where distance is sqrt(dSize² + dLien² + dNonAccrual²), dSize = |log2 of the fair-value ratio|, dLien = |difference in first-lien share| ÷ 0.10 and dNonAccrual = |difference in non-accrual rate| ÷ 0.01. No SIC filter, because EDGAR assigns ARCC and BXSL none.
terms.source: This site's own BDC distance, applied to the 50 listed BDCs only
terms.workingRef: frontend/lib/valuation.js (selectComparables, minPool 6, keep 8; the BDC distance callback lands with the Lenders view); blueprint v2 §4.5
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (This site's own peer rule for BDCs. From...)

terms.popup: An average that tames big outliers: n ÷ Σ(1/x). Used to aggregate peer multiples, because a plain mean of ratios is dragged up by one extreme value.
terms.definition: n ÷ Σ(1/x), the course's headline aggregate for a peer multiple (Liu, Nissim and Thomas, equation 3). Positive inputs only: negative and zero multiples are excluded before averaging. The site reports it beside the median and the plain mean for the BDC peer set.
terms.source: Liu, Nissim and Thomas, 'Equity Valuation Using Multiples' (2002), equation 3; this site's own peer aggregate
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (n ÷ Σ(1/x), the course's headline aggreg...)

terms.popup: The share of the loan book marked below 80 cents on the dollar: cost of third-party debt with FV/cost under 0.80 ÷ cost of third-party debt. The private analogue of the leveraged-loan 'under-80' ratio.
terms.definition: Computed per loan from the data set or instance. Liquid reference: 4.5% / $62.8B of the loan index at Dec 31 2023, 7.4% / $103.4B at the Dec 31 2022 peak. Every such loan also appears on the watchlist.
terms.source: This site's own per-loan rule on the parsed schedule of investments; PitchBook 2023 Annual Global Private Debt Report for the loan-index reference figures

terms.popup: The holdings that need a second look: every loan on non-accrual, every third-party loan marked under 0.80, and every loan paying PIK, each with the loss so far (cost − fair value).
terms.definition: Table L9 in the per-BDC drill-down, built from the schedule with the non-accrual footnote, FV/cost and the PIK flag. Not a rating; a filter.
terms.source: This site's own filter for the per-BDC drill-down

terms.popup: Total debt divided by trailing-twelve-month EBITDA: how many years of cash earnings it would take to repay the debt. S&P calls under 1.5x minimal and over 5x highly leveraged.
terms.definition: EBITDA = operating income + depreciation and amortization, LTM. S&P Table 2 bands: minimal under 1.5x, modest 1.5-2x, intermediate 2-3x, significant 3-4x, aggressive 4-5x, highly leveraged over 5x. Bank guidance capped underwriting near 6x; a unitranche may attach at 6.0-7.0x.
terms.source: S&P 2009 corporate ratings criteria, financial-risk matrix Table 2 (efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/44676); MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets
terms.whereUsed: Underwriting: Leverage & coverage card; chart U1

terms.popup: Debt minus cash, divided by EBITDA. The cleaner leverage measure for a cash-rich company; the one the site's existing ratio catalog already computes.
terms.definition: Net debt ÷ annualized EBITDA, computed for every covered operating company from tagged balances. Borrower net leverage for BDC portfolios is disclosed-only, from the 8-K release, never computed.
terms.source: This site's own ratio catalog (net debt ÷ annualized EBITDA); this site's disclosed-only rule for BDC borrowers
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Net debt ÷ annualized EBITDA, computed f...)

terms.popup: S&P's main cash-flow leverage ratio: funds from operations as a percentage of debt. Over 60% is minimal risk, under 12% highly leveraged.
terms.definition: S&P Table 2 bands: minimal over 60%, modest 45-60, intermediate 30-45, significant 20-30, aggressive 12-20, highly leveraged under 12%. FFO is S&P's operating-cash-flow measure before working capital; its component definition is not in the folder and the site labels the ratio by S&P's name.
terms.source: S&P 2009 corporate ratings criteria, financial-risk matrix Table 2 (efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/44676)

terms.popup: EBIT or EBITDA divided by interest expense: how many times earnings cover the interest bill. Below about 1x a company is not earning its interest. No document in the folder states a floor, so none is drawn.
terms.definition: Earnings divided by interest expense, computed three ways for every covered company: on EBIT, on EBITDA and on NOPAT. Drawn on a log axis in chart U1 against debt/EBITDA. Borrower interest coverage for BDC portfolios is disclosed-only.
terms.source: This site's own ratio catalog (EBIT, EBITDA and NOPAT over interest expense)
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Earnings divided by interest expense, co...)

terms.popup: Fixed-charge coverage ratio: (EBITDA minus capex minus cash taxes) over (cash interest plus mandatory amortization). A second maintenance covenant in about one in five private loans, beside the total-leverage test (Proskauer, 2021).
terms.definition: Site formula in the non-GAAP form: (EBITDA − capex − cash taxes) ÷ (cash interest + mandatory amortization). Proskauer: 99% of 2021 private credit loans had at least one maintenance covenant, typically total leverage, and 21% had two or more, 'i.e., a total leverage ratio and fixed charge coverage ratio covenant'.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets (structural protections section); standard loan-covenant definition
terms.fixNote: popup replaced per the refuter

terms.popup: S&P's six-step ladder from minimal to highly leveraged, set by debt/EBITDA and FFO/debt. The site uses it to place every covered company and to measure covenant headroom.
terms.definition: 'Criteria Methodology: Business Risk/Financial Risk Matrix Expanded' (May 27, 2009), Table 2 Financial Risk Indicative Ratios (Corporates): FFO/debt >60 / 45-60 / 30-45 / 20-30 / 12-20 / <12%; debt/EBITDA <1.5 / 1.5-2 / 2-3 / 3-4 / 4-5 / >5x; debt/capital <25 / 25-35 / 35-45 / 45-50 / 50-60 / >60%. S&P: indicative, 'not meant to be precise indications or guarantees'.
terms.source: S&P 2009 corporate ratings criteria, financial-risk matrix (efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/44676)
terms.whereUsed: Underwriting ladder; chart U1 quadrant lines

terms.popup: The 2013 US bank regulators' guidance that treated more than 6x debt/EBITDA as a red flag for bank underwriting. Private lenders are not bound by it, which is why they can attach higher.
terms.definition: Proskauer: 'Guidance issued by the U.S. federal banking agencies generally limited how much leverage a bank could underwrite in a leverage loan transaction to 6x debt to EBITDA, with EBITDA calculated on the basis of a standard definition.' On the site the 6.0x line is drawn only for companies at or above 4.0x, as a second sub-investment-grade ladder.
terms.source: Interagency Guidance on Leveraged Lending (OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, March 2013); MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets, footnote 27

terms.popup: The level of leverage at which a lender's claim begins. A bank loan attaches at 4.5-5.0x EBITDA; a unitranche may attach at 6.0-7.0x, so equity and junior debt must be wiped out first before it loses.
terms.definition: Proskauer: 'most private credit loans are at a balance sheet attachment point whereby any value deterioration is first borne by equity (the sponsor), next by unsecured and junior secured debt, and only then by the senior secured unitranche.' Average private credit leverage at closing in 2021 was 5.2x; S&P's B- issuers 7.2x.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets

terms.popup: How far a company is from the next leverage band, in turns of EBITDA and in the earnings drop that would get it there. Labeled synthetic: real covenants live in the credit agreement, which the site cannot see.
terms.definition: Distance to the next S&P band and, for sub-investment-grade names, to 6.0x, expressed as turns and as the percentage EBITDA decline that reaches it. Drawn as gauges in chart U4.
terms.source: This site's own construction on the S&P financial-risk bands and the 6.0x leveraged-lending line

terms.popup: Debt through a lender's tranche ÷ the borrower's enterprise value. A 50% LTV means the company's value would have to halve before the lender loses. BXSL's average: 51.9%.
terms.definition: BXSL: 'Loan-to-value is calculated as the current total net debt through each respective loan tranche divided by the estimated enterprise value of the portfolio company as of the most recent quarter-end', weighted by fair value across private debt investments. For BDC portfolios it is disclosed-only; for covered companies the site computes net debt ÷ EV.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 ('Average loan-to-value (LTV)' in the portfolio table)
terms.whereUsed: Underwriting: Priority & recovery card; BDC disclosed-only fields

terms.popup: (Cash + undrawn revolver + last-twelve-month free cash flow) ÷ (debt due in 12 months + lease payments). Under 1.0× the company must refinance to get through the year.
terms.definition: Built from LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity (11 of 130 tagged), LesseeOperatingLeaseLiabilityPaymentsDue (103), InterestPaidNet or InterestPaid (107) and the 12-month maturity concept. Chart U3.
terms.source: SEC XBRL frames, CY2025Q4I, across the 130 covered companies (LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity, LesseeOperatingLeaseLiabilityPaymentsDue, InterestPaidNet); this site's own construction

terms.popup: Who gets paid first when a borrower fails: secured lenders, then unsecured, then subordinated, then equity. A lender's place in that queue matters more than its interest rate.
terms.definition: Read from the capital stack and the loan's lien. Proskauer's order of loss: equity first, then unsecured and junior secured debt, then the senior secured unitranche. On the Underwriting card: secured share where tagged and LongTermDebtFairValue versus carrying value as the market's mark.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets; standard capital-structure vocabulary

terms.popup: The share of principal a lender gets back after a default, through repayment, restructuring or sale of the collateral. Higher priority and lower LTV mean higher recovery.
terms.definition: Proskauer: private lenders use 'the workout and restructuring toolbox to the fullest extent to maximize their recoveries at or near par'. The site does not compute recovery; the card shows the inputs (LTV, secured share, market mark on the debt) and the loss so far on the BDC watchlist (cost − fair value).
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets; standard credit vocabulary

terms.popup: What the whole business is worth to all its funders: equity value plus net debt. Lenders compare their loan with it (loan-to-value) because it is the pot that repays them if the company is sold.
terms.definition: BXSL's valuation note: 'An enterprise value ("EV") analysis is generally performed to determine the value of equity investments, control debt investments and non-control debt investments that are credit-impaired', using multiples of EBITDA or discounted cash flows. On the site, EV for a covered company comes from the existing bridge from market value to enterprise value: equity plus debt, preferred and minority interest, less financial assets in the net-debt view.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 (valuation note); this site's own enterprise-value bridge
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (BXSL's valuation note: 'An enterprise va...)

terms.popup: The most recent four quarters added together. Used for EBITDA, free cash flow and interest so that ratios are not distorted by one seasonal quarter.
terms.definition: The site's statements feed builds annual, quarterly and LTM views of every covered company; EBITDA for the Underwriting view is operating income + D&A over the LTM window. Also called trailing twelve months (TTM) in the market feed.
terms.source: Standard definition; this site's own statements feed for the LTM window
terms.workingRef: scripts/lib/statements.mjs (the annual, quarterly and LTM views)
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (The site's statements feed builds annual...)

terms.popup: A forward-looking SOFR for one or three months ahead, set by CME from SOFR futures. Most loans reset off it, but FRED does not carry it, so the site uses the 90-day average SOFR as the stand-in.
terms.definition: CME Group's forward-looking term rates derived from SOFR futures, published for several tenors. Private loans and BDC credit facilities reset off a term SOFR tenor plus a margin: BXSL's facilities priced off 'three-month Term SOFR' and 'one-month Term SOFR'. FRED publishes overnight SOFR and its compounded averages, not the CME term rates, so the site's SOFR90DAYAVG tile is a stand-in and says so.
terms.source: CME Group Term SOFR reference rates page (cmegroup.com/market-data/cme-group-benchmark-administration/term-sofr.html); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 (accession 0001736035-26-000016), credit-facility note
terms.whereUsed: SOFR tile caveat; M2 yield stack; spread-over-base popups

terms.popup: The UK's overnight sterling rate, published by the Bank of England. Sterling loans in a BDC book reset off SONIA instead of SOFR, so spreads on the page are 'over base', not 'over SOFR'.
terms.definition: The Bank of England's overnight sterling benchmark. BDC schedules mark sterling loans as referenced to 'Sterling Overnight Interbank Average Rate ("SONIA" or "S")', which is why the site labels spreads as bps over base rather than over SOFR.
terms.source: Bank of England SONIA page (bankofengland.co.uk/markets/sonia-benchmark); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 schedule footnote 2
terms.whereUsed: Spread-over-base popups; schedule parser base-rate column

terms.popup: The euro area's interbank term rate, published by EMMI. Euro loans in a BDC book reset off EURIBOR, so a spread over base means over EURIBOR for them, not over SOFR.
terms.definition: The euro-area term benchmark administered by the European Money Markets Institute. BDC schedules mark euro loans as referenced to 'Euro Interbank Offer Rate ("Euribor" or "E")'. One of the three base rates (SOFR, SONIA, EURIBOR) behind the site's 'bps over base' label.
terms.source: EMMI EURIBOR page (emmi-benchmarks.eu/benchmarks/euribor); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 schedule footnote 2
terms.whereUsed: Spread-over-base popups; schedule parser base-rate column

terms.expansion: earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization
terms.popup: Operating profit with depreciation and amortization added back: the rough cash earnings lenders size debt against. Every leverage and coverage ratio in credit uses it, and add-backs can inflate it.
terms.definition: On this site, EBITDA for a covered company is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, computed from tagged statements and never adjusted. For BDC borrowers it is disclosed-only: BXSL reports a weighted average annual EBITDA for its portfolio companies in the 10-Q. The MFA/Proskauer paper notes that EBITDA add-backs (run-rate synergies, non-recurring costs) 'can materially distort actual earnings if not realized' and that private lenders cap them.
terms.source: This site's own ratio catalog (EBITDA and debt/EBITDA); BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30; MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets, structural protections section
terms.whereUsed: Underwriting cards; debt/EBITDA and net debt/EBITDA popups; section 15 leverage rows
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (On this site, EBITDA for a covered compa...)

terms.popup: A covenant tested only when the borrower acts: takes on more debt, pays a dividend, sells assets. It cannot trip on its own, so a cov-lite loan with only incurrence tests gives lenders no early seat at the table.
terms.definition: A restriction checked at the moment a borrower does something the loan agreement limits (incurring debt, making a restricted payment, selling assets), as opposed to a maintenance covenant, which is tested every quarter whether or not the borrower acts. Broadly syndicated cov-lite loans carry incurrence covenants only; the MFA/Proskauer paper reports that 99% of private credit loans in 2021 had at least one financial maintenance covenant, which is the structural difference the Underwriting view describes.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets, structural protections section; the incurrence/maintenance distinction is standard loan-documentation vocabulary
terms.whereUsed: Cov-lite and maintenance-covenant popups; Underwriting covenant headroom card

terms.popup: The arranging bank's right to raise the price or tighten the terms of a syndicated loan if investors will not buy it as first offered. Private lenders commit without it, which is the certainty sponsors pay for.
terms.definition: MFA/Proskauer: market flex terms are 'key terms pre-agreed to by the lead bank and the private equity sponsor which the lead bank can change to the extent necessary to permit the lead bank to sell down the loan', including 'an increase in economics (such as a higher interest rate) or tighter documentation terms'. Direct lenders 'commit fully without market flex', so their terms are more heavily negotiated up front.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets, syndication section
terms.whereUsed: Syndication and club-deal popups; Market view deal-flow blurb

terms.popup: The most junior claim that still gets paid something in a restructuring, so it ends up owning the company. Distressed funds buy it at a discount to take control.
terms.definition: PitchBook: distressed strategies 'likely involve identification of the "fulcrum" security, or the most subordinated part of the capital stack to be paid back in a bankruptcy or other restructuring, which can trade at steep discounts to net asset value'. Where the fulcrum sits depends on the enterprise value at the time of the restructuring, which is why loan-to-value and priority matter to a lender before any default.
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, 'Fund type definitions'
terms.whereUsed: Distressed debt popup; Underwriting priority and recovery card

terms.popup: An acquisition bolted onto a sponsor-owned platform company, usually funded by drawing a delayed-draw term loan or an incremental facility. Buy-and-build strategies string several together.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'Many larger LBOs now involve buy-and-build strategies where sponsors acquire a platform and expand via multiple add-ons.' For the lender, each add-on is a draw on committed but unfunded capital (the delayed-draw term loan rows in a BDC's commitments table) and a change in the borrower's leverage and EBITDA at once.
terms.source: PitchBook Q3 2025 Analyst Note: From Peak to Pivot
terms.whereUsed: Delayed-draw and unfunded-commitment popups; LCD deal-flow series

terms.popup: New debt raised by a company so its owner can pay itself a dividend. Sponsors use it to return cash when exits are slow; for the lender it adds leverage without adding earnings.
terms.definition: A refinancing whose proceeds go to the shareholders rather than the business. PitchBook's Q3 2026 Quantitative Perspectives: 'As exit activity has fallen short of generating adequate liquidity, managers have leaned on dividend recapitalizations despite elevated financing' costs (figures 59-60 chart sponsored dividend recap deal value against the B-rated loan index). LCD counts it under 'recapitalization' in its use-of-proceeds split.
terms.source: PitchBook Q3 2026 Quantitative Perspectives: US Market Insights (figures 59-60); LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026, slide 8 (use-of-proceeds categories)

terms.popup: The manager of a private fund: it raises the money, picks the loans, controls when capital is called and returned, and earns the management fee and carried interest.
terms.definition: The partner in a limited-partnership fund who runs it, as against the LPs who supply the capital. PitchBook: 'a GP that controls when assets are bought and sold is imperative' to a portfolio of illiquid investments. For a BDC the equivalent is the external adviser; internally managed BDCs have none.
terms.source: PitchBook Q3 2024 Analyst Note: The Evergreen Evolution; PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Fund-level cash flow and performance metrics'
terms.whereUsed: Fundraising and fee series; externally managed popup

terms.popup: An investor in a private fund, such as a pension plan or insurer. LPs commit capital, the manager calls it over time, and their liability is limited to what they committed.
terms.definition: The capital providers in a limited-partnership fund. IRR and the fund multiples are computed from the LPs' cash flows: 'capital calls (outflows from the LPs) and distributions (inflows to the LPs)'. The PitchBook workbook's sources-of-capital sheet counts commitments by LP type (pensions the largest).
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Internal rate of return'; PitchBook Fund Overview workbook, sources of capital sheet (downloaded 2026-09-10)

terms.popup: The traditional private fund: investors commit capital, the manager calls it down over a few years, and the fund winds up after about ten. PitchBook's benchmarks and fundraising counts cover only these.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'the traditional PE drawdown, finite-life fund structure' with 'a relatively long-term horizon, typically 10+ years'. Its benchmarks are built from 'private, closed-end drawdown fund cash flows and returns'; evergreen or canceled funds are excluded. The 2024 report's fundraising figures count 'committed capital ... closed by traditional drawdown funds'.
terms.source: PitchBook Q3 2024 Analyst Note: The Evergreen Evolution; PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025); PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report

terms.popup: A fund with no end date: investors can buy in at intervals and redeem within limits, and capital is recycled into new loans instead of returned. Non-traded BDCs and interval funds are the private credit versions.
terms.definition: PitchBook uses 'evergreen', 'perpetual capital' and 'semi-liquid' interchangeably for 'funds that allow investors to buy in at periodic intervals, have some provision for intermittent liquidity, and/or have no predetermined end', which 'can operate indefinitely by recycling capital into new deals instead of distributing the capital to LPs'. They sit outside the drawdown-fund benchmarks and fundraising counts, and the 2024 report's $2.2 trillion AUM figure (as of June 30, 2024) includes them.
terms.source: PitchBook Q3 2024 Analyst Note: The Evergreen Evolution, 'A note on terminology'; PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report

terms.popup: PitchBook's word for the largest funds in a strategy, the top size bucket in its fundraising charts. A few of them can carry a year's fundraising total, so the fund count matters as much as the dollars.
terms.definition: The largest size class in PitchBook's fundraising reports (the '$5B+' bucket in the Q2 2026 global fundraising report's size charts). The 2024 private debt report tracks 'capital raised by megafunds' as its own line and notes a 'larger crop of megafunds that have stayed open and rolled into the new calendar year'. The site draws the report's own series and does not define a threshold of its own.
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report; PitchBook 2023 Annual Global Private Debt Report; PitchBook Q2 2026 Global Private Market Fundraising Report size buckets

terms.popup: The steady yearly growth rate that would take a series from its first value to its last: (end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ years) − 1. PitchBook quotes AUM growth this way.
terms.definition: The geometric average growth rate over a span, so that compounding at it for the whole span reproduces the end value. PitchBook's 2024 report headline: 'Global direct lending AUM hits $678.5 billion, a 22.2% 10-year CAGR' (AUM as of June 30, 2024). The site computes it only over series it holds in full, never from two quoted endpoints.
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report; standard formula

terms.popup: The annual return that makes a fund's capital calls and distributions net to zero. It rewards getting money back early. Not computed on this site; benchmark values are drawn as dated points only.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'the annualized rate of return that makes the net present value (NPV) of all cash flows from a fund equal to zero', accounting for the timing of capital calls and distributions; interim IRRs treat the remaining NAV as a final distribution, and are of limited meaning early in a fund's life. By the site's own rule, no fund-level IRR is computed here.
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Internal rate of return'
terms.whereUsed: Benchmark reference points; fund metrics glossary (reference only)

terms.popup: Everything a fund has returned plus what it still holds, divided by the capital paid in. TVPI = DPI + RVPI. A multiple, so it ignores how long the money was out. Not computed on this site.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'A measurement of both the realized and unrealized value of a fund as a proportion of the total paid-in, or contributed, capital. Also known as the investment multiple, TVPI can be found by adding together the DPI and RVPI of a fund.' Benchmarks state multiples net of fees and carry.
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Multiples'
terms.whereUsed: Benchmark reference points; fund metrics glossary (reference only)

terms.popup: Cash actually returned to investors divided by the capital they paid in. The realization multiple: the part of a fund's return that is no longer an estimate. Not computed on this site.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'A measurement of the capital that has been distributed back to LPs as a proportion of the total paid-in, or contributed, capital. DPI is also known as the cash-on-cash multiple or the realization multiple.' As a fund liquidates, 'the DPI will converge toward the TVPI, and the RVPI will approach zero.'
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Multiples'
terms.whereUsed: Benchmark reference points; fund metrics glossary (reference only)

terms.popup: What a fund still holds, at the manager's marks, divided by the capital paid in. The unrealized part of the multiple; it should fall toward zero as the fund winds up. Not computed on this site.
terms.definition: PitchBook: 'A measurement of a fund's unrealized value (also known as NAV) as a proportion of the total paid-in, or contributed, capital.' It is the component of TVPI that depends on valuation rather than cash.
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Multiples'
terms.whereUsed: Benchmark reference points; fund metrics glossary (reference only)

terms.popup: What the same cash flows would have earned in a public index. The Kaplan-Schoar version is a ratio: above 1.0× the fund beat the index. Direct alpha is the annualized form. Not computed on this site.
terms.definition: PitchBook: PMEs 'are a method of adjusting PE cash flows, and NAVs in the case of still-active funds, as if they had been invested in a public market index': each capital call buys the index, each distribution sells it. 'The KS-PME calculates a multiple of invested capital in a private fund relative to what it would have been in a public market index'; direct alpha annualizes the same comparison with XIRR.
terms.source: PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology (September 29, 2025), 'Public market equivalents (PMEs)'
terms.whereUsed: Benchmark reference points; fund metrics glossary (reference only)

terms.popup: The private-markets data vendor behind the fundraising, AUM, dry-powder and fund-performance series here, drawn from its annual private debt reports and a fund-overview workbook. Its LCD unit covers the loan market.
terms.definition: The source of every ingested and hand-keyed capital series on the Market view: the annual global private debt reports (2021-2024 editions), the Quantitative Perspectives issues, the Q2 2026 global fundraising report, the benchmarking methodology and the fund-overview workbook (population 'Access Point: All; Fund Category: All; Fund Size: All; Vintage: All; USD', downloaded 2026-09-10). Each series carries its edition and as-of date on the chart.
terms.source: The study material: 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, Q3 2026 Quantitative Perspectives: US Market Insights, Q2 2026 Global Private Market Fundraising Report, PitchBook Fund Benchmarks: Data and Methodology, and the PitchBook Fund Overview workbook (downloaded 2026-09-10)
terms.whereUsed: Every capital and fund-performance caption and footer

terms.popup: PitchBook's loan-market news and data unit. Its monthly US private credit monitor and daily leveraged loan playbook supply the deal-flow, spread, BDC-portfolio and takeout series here.
terms.definition: Leveraged Commentary & Data, the loan-market service now inside PitchBook. The August 2026 US private credit monitor (43 slides, 31 charts) supplies 89 series, from new-issue direct-lending volume and spread buckets to BDC portfolio spread distributions, maturity walls and cost-weighted all-in yields; the September 10 2026 daily playbook supplies index levels such as the LL100. LCD's BDC population is 'over 100 BDC portfolios', which implies non-listed funds, so it is compared with the site's listed composite by direction, never by level.
terms.source: LCD US Private Credit Monitor, August 2026 (slide 43 methodology); PitchBook LCD US Leveraged Loan Daily Playbook, September 10, 2026
terms.whereUsed: Every LCD-sourced chart footer; M1 reference dot; M4 histogram

aliases: ICE BofA US High Yield Index
terms.popup: The bond index family behind the six spread and yield tiles. FRED carries the index-level option-adjusted spreads and effective yields, but only three years of history since April 2026.
terms.definition: Indices of US-dollar corporate bonds maintained by Intercontinental Exchange, weighted by market capitalization and rated on an average of Moody's, S&P and Fitch. FRED serves the US High Yield Index (BAMLH0A0HYM2 and its BB, B and CCC subsets), the US Corporate Index (BAMLC0A0CM) and the high-yield effective yield (BAMLH0A0HYM2EY). Each FRED page states: 'Starting in April 2026, this series will only include 3 years of observations', which is why the tiles say '3-year'.
terms.source: FRED series pages for BAMLH0A0HYM2, BAMLC0A0CM and BAMLH0A0HYM2EY, Notes block (fetched 2026-09-11)

aliases: Morningstar LSTA US Leveraged Loan Index
terms.popup: The index family that prices the syndicated loan market: the full Leveraged Loan Index and the LL100 of the hundred largest loans. PitchBook uses it as the public stand-in for private debt returns.
terms.definition: Indices of US institutional leveraged loans administered by Morningstar with the Loan Syndications and Trading Association, quoted as weighted average bid prices and as returns split into interest and market components. LCD's playbook quotes the LL100 daily; PitchBook's 2024 report calls the index 'a good proxy for private debt returns, particularly direct lending'.
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report; PitchBook LCD US Leveraged Loan Daily Playbook, September 10, 2026
terms.whereUsed: Loan index references; mark (FV/cost) comparison; M4 caption

terms.popup: The trade body for alternative asset managers. With Proskauer it wrote the paper the Underwriting view leans on for covenant incidence, attachment points and how private credit differs from syndicated loans.
terms.definition: The trade association of alternative asset managers. Its white paper 'The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets', 'Prepared by Managed Funds Association and The Private Credit Group of Proskauer Rose LLP', is the source for the site's statements about maintenance covenants (99% of private loans in 2021), market flex, club deals and attachment points. It is an industry advocacy document and is cited as such.
terms.source: MFA and Proskauer, The Role of Private Credit in U.S. Capital Markets
terms.whereUsed: Underwriting view reference notes; cov-lite, club deal, attachment point popups

terms.popup: A US credit rating agency whose private credit default figures this site draws as a separate series with its own definition, never averaged with Proskauer's, Fitch's or Moody's.
terms.definition: One of the four sources of a private credit default rate the site treats separately (Proskauer, KBRA, Fitch and Moody's), each with its own definition and population, never averaged into a market-wide rate. Where a KBRA rating action appears in the hyperscaler ledger it is a row with a URL, never a number.

terms.popup: One of the three big rating agencies. Its Baa grade is the lowest investment-grade band, and FRED's BAA10Y is Moody's seasoned Baa corporate yield minus the 10-year Treasury.
terms.definition: Rating agency whose Baa band is the lowest investment-grade band, equal to BBB at S&P and Fitch; Ba and below is speculative grade. ICE BofA assigns index membership on an average of Moody's, S&P and Fitch. The site draws Moody's private credit default figures as their own series and records Moody's rating actions as rows, never as numbers.
terms.source: FRED series page for BAA10Y (Moody's Seasoned Baa Corporate Bond Yield Relative to Yield on 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity), fetched 2026-09-11; FRED Notes for BAMLH0A0HYM2 (rating average)

terms.popup: One of the three big rating agencies, on the AAA-to-D scale shared with S&P. Its private credit default count is drawn here as its own series, never averaged with the others.
terms.definition: Rating agency on the AAA-to-D scale shared with S&P: BBB- is the lowest investment-grade rating and BB+ the highest speculative grade. ICE BofA uses an average of Moody's, S&P and Fitch for index membership. Fitch's private credit default measure has its own definition and population and is one of the four the site keeps apart.
terms.source: FRED Notes for BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ratings averaged across Moody's, S&P and Fitch), fetched 2026-09-11

terms.definition: Rating agency on the AAA-to-D scale. Two uses on this site: the 2009 corporate ratings matrix, whose Table 2 bands debt/EBITDA from minimal (under 1.5x) to highly leveraged (over 5x) and gives FFO/debt bands alongside; and rating actions on the hyperscaler ledger, where S&P text is archived because its pages answer 403 to fetchers.

On chart M8 its monthly closes (price) and adjusted closes (total return) over five years are rebased to 100 and drawn against SRLN or BKLN; because BDCs pay high distributions the two lines diverge, and the caption says which is shown. terms.definition: An exchange-traded fund of syndicated senior loans (Yahoo's chart feed names it 'Invesco Senior Loan ETF', 61 monthly points over five years, fetched 2026-09-11). terms.definition: Yahoo's chart feed returns two series per month: close (the traded price) and adjclose (indicators.adjclose), which folds every dividend and split back into the history. Chart M8's total-return toggle uses the adjusted close and its price toggle the plain close; the caption states which. Because the adjustment re-scales past values, the adjusted series changes each time a distribution is paid.
