terms.popup: Each series divided by its own first value and multiplied by 100, so two prices that start at different levels can be read as growth from a common start. 125 means up 25% since the first month.
terms.definition: Index construction: value_t ÷ value_0 × 100 for every series on the chart, with the same first month for all. Chart M8 rebases BIZD and the loan ETF to 100 at the first month of the five-year window, in both the price and the total-return views. The ending values are the five-year change the caption quotes.
terms.source: Standard index construction; this site's own chart method

terms.popup: Lending against property: mostly direct loans for real estate acquisitions, sometimes trading securitized property loans. One of PitchBook's nine private debt fund types.
terms.definition: PitchBook fund type definition: 'The most common real estate debt strategy is direct lending for real estate acquisitions but may also include the buying and selling of securitized real estate loans in the secondary market. Risk profiles vary based on the nature of the underlying assets.' Drawn as one series of the US private debt capital raised by type stack (chart29).
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, 'Fund type definitions'

terms.popup: Long-dated lending to infrastructure projects, both new builds and existing assets. Terms can run thirty years or more because the assets last that long. One of PitchBook's nine private debt fund types.
terms.definition: PitchBook fund type definition: 'Debt used for infrastructure development (for example, greenfield) and investment in existing assets (for example, brownfield), generally with longer terms (30-plus years) due to the extended useful life of the assets.' Drawn as one series of the US private debt capital raised by type stack (chart29).
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, 'Fund type definitions'

terms.popup: Short-term loans made while longer financing is arranged, also called swing loans. One of PitchBook's nine private debt fund types.
terms.definition: PitchBook fund type definition: 'Private debt funds that provide short-term loans, also called swing loans, made in anticipation of intermediate-term or long-term financing.' Drawn as one series of the US private debt capital raised by type stack (chart29).
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, 'Fund type definitions'

terms.popup: PitchBook's catch-all fund type, labeled 'Debt' on the chart: credit funds with a broad mandate across the capital structure and sub-strategies, often holding public debt as well as private.
terms.definition: PitchBook fund type definition: 'General-purpose credit funds with broad mandates to invest across the debt capital structure, substrategies, and verticals to capture the entire opportunity set in private credit. These funds will often invest in public debt as well as private debt on a dynamic and opportunistic basis.' The chart29 series is labeled simply 'Debt', which is why the legend carries this popup.
terms.source: PitchBook 2024 Annual Global Private Debt Report, 'Fund type definitions'

terms.popup: The quarter's net investment income divided by the weighted average shares: the earnings that fund the dividend, per share. Read it against the regular dividend per share.
terms.definition: Tagged as InvestmentCompanyInvestmentIncomeLossPerShare, year-to-date for most filers, so the site differences the prior year-to-date value within the fiscal year to get the quarter. Cross-check: after-tax NII ÷ weighted basic shares should match within a cent. Present on all six probed BDCs; three-month coverage in frames CY2026Q2 is 18 of 50.
terms.source: us-gaap investment-company taxonomy element InvestmentCompanyInvestmentIncomeLossPerShare, tagged by ARCC, BXSL, MAIN, OBDC, FSK and GBDC on SEC EDGAR companyfacts (checked 2026-09-10)

terms.popup: Annualized net investment income divided by average net assets: what the book earns for shareholders before marks. The BDC analogue of return on equity from earnings alone.
terms.definition: 4 × quarterly after-tax NII ÷ average net assets over the quarter. Never the tagged InvestmentCompanyInvestmentIncomeLossRatio, because filers differ on whether it is annualized (BXSL annualizes it, MAIN does not). Compare with the dividend yield on NAV and with the total return on NAV, which adds realized and unrealized gains.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements NetInvestmentIncome and StockholdersEquity on SEC EDGAR companyfacts; this site's own ratio

terms.popup: What the BDC pays on its own borrowings, as a weighted average rate. The other half of its margin: portfolio yield minus cost of debt is what leverage adds.
terms.definition: The tagged DebtWeightedAverageInterestRate (unit pure) where the filer reports it, otherwise interest expense ÷ average debt over the quarter, annualized, labeled as derived. Unsecured notes are fixed-rate and SPV or revolver borrowings float, so the mix in the liability ladder drives how fast this rate follows SOFR.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element DebtWeightedAverageInterestRate, tagged by ARCC and FSK on SEC EDGAR companyfacts (checked 2026-09-10); otherwise the 10-Q debt note
terms.whereUsed: Scorecard; net interest margin; liability ladder

terms.popup: Weighted-average yield on the debt portfolio at cost minus the BDC's cost of debt, in percentage points. The spread the BDC keeps for taking credit risk with borrowed money.
terms.definition: Weighted-average yield at cost − cost of debt, both from the scorecard. Because most BDC loans float and part of the liability stack is fixed, the margin widens when base rates rise and narrows as they fall; the Item 3 interest-rate sensitivity table shows the same effect in dollars per 100 bps.
terms.source: This site's own ratio on the scorecard's yield at cost and cost of debt; BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30, Item 3, for the sensitivity table

terms.popup: Trailing twelve months of distributions divided by the share price. For BDCs it runs near ten percent, which is why price and total return diverge so much on chart M8.
terms.definition: From the market feed's dividendYieldTTM (a fraction) on /api/comps; cross-checked against the trailing four quarters of tagged distributions per share ÷ price. The feed sample on 2026-09-10: ARCC 9.45%, BXSL 12.0%, MAIN 6.5%. A yield well above the peer median with coverage under 1.0× is the market pricing a cut.
terms.source: Finnhub stock/metric currentDividendYieldTTM (checked 2026-09-10)

terms.expansion: total investment income yield on average cost
terms.popup: Annualized total investment income divided by the average portfolio at cost. Interest plus dividends, fees and PIK over everything held, so it is broader than the yield on debt investments.
terms.definition: 4 × quarterly GrossInvestmentIncomeOperating ÷ average InvestmentOwnedAtCost, a quarterly series from companyfacts with no extra downloads (tagged by 40 of 50 in frames). Named this way because the numerator is not only interest (PIK, structuring fees, dividends and other income are in the tag) and the denominator includes equity and vehicle cost. An interest-only yield is drawn only where the interest tag is at least half of the total.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements GrossInvestmentIncomeOperating and InvestmentOwnedAtCost on SEC EDGAR companyfacts (tagged by 40 of 50 in frames); this site's own composite ratio
terms.whereUsed: Scorecard; M2 yield stack (composite line); composite strip L10

terms.popup: The weighted-average yield of the loans the BDC made this quarter, as stated in its 10-Q. Disclosed-only: the site prints the filer's sentence and never computes it.
terms.definition: BXSL's 10-Q line 'Weighted average yield of new investments' beside the yield on the whole portfolio. Read with the yield on exits: when new loans yield less than the ones repaid, the portfolio yield is drifting down whatever SOFR does. Where a filer does not state it, the cell is empty and labeled 'not disclosed in this filing'.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 ('Weighted average yield of new investments'); this site's disclosed-only rule

aliases: yield on investments fully sold or paid down
terms.popup: The weighted-average yield of the loans repaid or sold this quarter, as stated in the 10-Q. Disclosed-only. Higher than the yield on new loans means the book is being refinanced cheaper.
terms.definition: BXSL's 10-Q line 'Weighted average yield on investments fully sold or paid down'. The gap between this and the yield on new investments is the repricing pressure on the portfolio. Printed from the filing sentence with the accession as provenance; never computed by the site.
terms.source: BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 ('yield on investments fully sold or paid down'); this site's disclosed-only rule

terms.popup: How the BDC grades its own loans, usually on a 1-to-5 scale, as a share of the portfolio. Disclosed-only and not comparable across BDCs, whose scales differ.
terms.definition: Each BDC's internal grading of its holdings, stated in the 10-Q as a share of fair value per grade. The scales are the filer's own and are not tagged in companyfacts, so the site prints the disclosed table with its sentence and never computes or pools the grades. A rising share in the lower grades leads non-accruals.
terms.source: The BDC's own 10-Q internal risk-rating table (not tagged on SEC EDGAR companyfacts, checked 2026-09-10); this site's disclosed-only rule

terms.popup: The colored edge on a scorecard row when a fixed rule trips: regular dividend coverage under 1.0× for two straight quarters, asset-coverage cushion under 15%, non-accruals over 3% of cost, or price/NAV below the universe's 25th percentile.
terms.definition: Four rules, each stated on hover with the value that tripped it: regular dividend coverage under 1.0× for two consecutive quarters; asset-coverage cushion under 15%; non-accruals over 3% of total investments at cost; price/NAV below the universe's 25th percentile as stored at refresh. The percentile rule replaces a fixed 0.9× line, which would mark more than half the universe when the sector median is near 0.80×. A stripe is a filter, not a rating.
terms.source: This site's own reading rules for the Lenders scorecard
terms.workingRef: the 25th-percentile line is read from composite.json
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Four rules, each stated on hover with th...)

terms.popup: The check a parsed schedule must pass before it is served: the sum of the loans read from the filing must match the tagged portfolio totals. Fail, and the site records the refusal with its reason instead of showing wrong numbers.
terms.definition: Applied per filer at refresh: Σ cost and Σ fair value of the parsed schedule of investments against InvestmentOwnedAtCost and InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue from companyfacts, within a stated tolerance, plus the count of holdings against the filer's prose ('Number of portfolio companies'). A filer that fails is recorded with the gate's reason and every schedule-based cell shows 'not yet parsed'; nothing from a failed parse reaches a composite.
terms.source: This site's own parse rule: the schedule of investments must reconcile to InvestmentOwnedAtCost and InvestmentOwnedAtFairValue on SEC EDGAR companyfacts
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Applied per filer at refresh: Σ cost and...)

terms.popup: Cash paid in the period for property and equipment, from the investing section of the cash-flow statement. Not the company's quoted capex, which may add finance leases or net out incentives.
terms.definition: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, or the filer's alternate tag (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets for Amazon and Applied Digital), three-month where tagged and otherwise differenced from year-to-date. It differs from management's headline: Microsoft and Meta add finance leases, Amazon nets incentives, CoreWeave counts construction in progress, and IREN's tag excludes GPU payments. The capex panel shows the tagged line and bridges to the company metric on hover.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment and PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets (xbrl.fasb.org); each filer's cash-flow statement

terms.popup: The last four quarters of tagged capex added together: the pace the balance sheet must fund over a year at the current tempo. Never the latest quarter times four.
terms.definition: Σ of the four most recent consecutive quarters of tagged capex, trailing twelve months. It needs four consecutive quarters on the same basis; a filer with a gap shows the run-rate as unavailable rather than annualizing one quarter.
terms.source: Standard trailing-twelve-month construction on the tagged capex line; this site's own rule

terms.popup: Capex divided by operating cash flow: the share of operating cash the build consumes. Above 1.0 the build is financed from the balance sheet or the market, not from operations.
terms.definition: Tagged capex ÷ NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities over the same period. Customer prepayments (Nebius, Oracle) sit inside operating cash flow and lower the ratio, so the sources-and-uses chart is the fuller picture.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities; this site's own ratio

terms.popup: Capex divided by depreciation and amortization: how much faster the asset base grows than it is consumed. Near 1.0 is maintenance; well above it is a build-out. A useful-life change moves the denominator without any change in spending.
terms.definition: Tagged capex ÷ D&A over the same period (the Depreciation tag alone for Microsoft, Alphabet and Oracle). The same ratio the Statement Analysis catalog computes for every covered company; on the build-out panel a change in useful lives, such as Microsoft's in July 2026, is labeled so the ratio is not read as a spending change.
terms.source: This site's own ratio catalog (capex ÷ depreciation and amortization); us-gaap taxonomy elements Depreciation and DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization
terms.whereUsed: Capex panel; Statement Analysis cash-flow group
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (Tagged capex ÷ D&A over the same period ...)

terms.popup: Capex plus buybacks, dividends and debt repaid, minus operating cash flow: the cash a company had to raise or draw down in the period. Positive means the market or the cash pile paid.
terms.definition: Site arithmetic on tagged cash-flow lines for one fiscal year: capex + buybacks + dividends + debt repaid − operating cash flow. It is not an agency's free-operating-cash-flow deficit, which is a forecast on the agency's own definitions. The sources chart shows which channel filled the gap.
terms.source: This site's own arithmetic on the tagged cash-flow lines (capex, buybacks, dividends, debt repaid, operating cash flow)
terms.whereUsed: Sources and uses panel; chart H4

terms.popup: A cash-flow bridge for one fiscal year. Sources: operating cash flow, debt raised, converts, equity and preferred, partner and customer funding, cash drawdown. Uses: capex, buybacks, dividends, debt repaid.
terms.definition: Every bar is a tagged cash-flow line or a hand-keyed row with its accession; finance-lease additions are non-cash and are drawn beside the sources, not inside them. Read the mix first, then the year-on-year shift in the mix: a build funded from operations one year and from debt the next is the story of the build-out monitor.
terms.source: Each filer's cash-flow statement and financing notes; this site's own chart method
terms.whereUsed: Sources and uses panel; charts H4-H5

terms.popup: A finance lease transfers most of the asset's economics to the tenant and is presented like debt; an operating lease is a right of use with rent expense. Moving new leases to operating cuts reported capex, not the commitment.
terms.definition: Both sit on the balance sheet as a liability and a right-of-use asset, but only the finance lease's additions count in a company's capex metric and only its liability reads like borrowing. Tags: FinanceLeaseLiability, OperatingLeaseLiability, RightOfUseAssetObtainedInExchangeForFinanceLeaseLiability. Microsoft said in July 2026 that most future data-center leases will be operating leases, outside its capex metric; the panel labels that policy change rather than reading it as a spending cut.
terms.source: ASC 842 (Leases); us-gaap taxonomy elements FinanceLeaseLiability, OperatingLeaseLiability and RightOfUseAssetObtainedInExchangeForFinanceLeaseLiability; the filer's leases note
terms.whereUsed: Debt, leases and obligations panel; chart H6

aliases: leases that have not yet commenced
terms.popup: Signed leases, mostly data centers, whose term has not started. Undiscounted future payments over terms up to twenty years; not debt and not on the balance sheet, but the forward commitment to the landlords.
terms.definition: Disclosed in the leases note as prose or, for Meta, tagged under UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligationBalanceSheetAmount. The panel draws each filer's figure beside its gross debt with the accession, never summed across filers because each defines the scope differently.
terms.source: ASC 842 leases-note disclosure of leases not yet commenced; us-gaap taxonomy element UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligationBalanceSheetAmount; the filer's leases note
terms.whereUsed: Debt, leases and obligations panel; chart H7

terms.popup: Non-cancelable promises to buy goods, services, capacity or power. Take-or-pay exposure that behaves like debt in a downturn. Each filer defines it differently, so the panel never sums it across companies.
terms.definition: From ContractualObligation, LongTermPurchaseCommitmentAmount, UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligationBalanceSheetAmount or the commitments table, whichever the filer uses. Amazon's table includes debt and leases; Meta's excludes uncommenced leases. Shown per filer with its own definition on hover.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements ContractualObligation, LongTermPurchaseCommitmentAmount and UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligationBalanceSheetAmount; the filer's commitments note
terms.whereUsed: Debt, leases and obligations panel; chart H7

terms.popup: Total principal of borrowings outstanding: the number the maturity ladder has to refinance. Face value, not carrying value, which can sit below face after an exchange premium.
terms.definition: DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount as the undimensioned total principal where tagged, otherwise current plus non-current debt. Face and carrying values differ where notes were issued or exchanged away from par, so the panel names which it shows.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount and LongTermDebt; the filer's debt note
terms.whereUsed: Debt panel; maturity ladder; net debt

terms.popup: Gross debt minus cash and marketable securities: borrowings after the cash that could repay them. Negative is net cash; a line crossing zero is the moment a company stops being a net creditor.
terms.definition: gross debt − cash − marketable securities, on tagged balances at each period end. Restricted cash (escrowed bond proceeds) is excluded and shown on hover. For covered operating companies the same figure comes from the site's ratio catalog, the single source the Underwriting view reads.
terms.source: This site's own definition: gross debt − cash − marketable securities, on tagged balances
terms.whereUsed: Debt panel; net debt to EBITDA; Underwriting leverage card
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (gross debt − cash − marketable securitie...)

terms.popup: Interest on borrowings during construction that is added to the asset's cost instead of being expensed. It lowers reported interest expense while cash interest is unchanged, so the coverage ratio adds it back.
terms.definition: InterestCostsCapitalized or InterestCostsCapitalizedAdjustment where tagged. Large capitalized interest means the debt is funding assets not yet earning; the build-out monitor's interest-coverage formula uses interest expense plus capitalized interest as its denominator so a build cannot flatter the ratio.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements InterestCostsCapitalized and InterestCostsCapitalizedAdjustment (ASC 835-20)

aliases: capex incurred but not yet paid
terms.popup: Property and equipment received but not yet paid for. A timing item that becomes cash capex next quarter and explains gaps between quoted and cash capex.
terms.definition: CapitalExpendituresIncurredButNotYetPaid, the non-cash disclosure in the cash-flow statement's supplemental section. It is why a quarter's cash capex can trail the equipment actually delivered, and why the bridge from the company's quoted capex to the tagged line needs it.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element CapitalExpendituresIncurredButNotYetPaid; the cash-flow statement's supplemental non-cash disclosures

terms.popup: Principal due by year. Near-term bars set against cash and undrawn facilities are the refinancing risk; the same picture the BDC maturity wall gives for a loan book.
terms.definition: LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipal buckets (next twelve months, years two to five, thereafter) or the note's table where the buckets are not tagged. Buckets are fiscal years for June and May filers; a ladder tagged only in the 10-K predates the year's issuance and is drawn hatched.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths through AfterYearFive; SEC XBRL frames, CY2025Q4I, across the 130 covered companies
terms.whereUsed: Debt panel; chart H8; Underwriting maturity wall card

terms.popup: A customer contract that obliges payment whether or not the capacity is used, pledged to lenders. It is why a speculative-grade borrower can carry an investment-grade project loan. Backlog is revenue, not cash.
terms.definition: The contract value and term as printed, with lender step-in rights where disclosed. The credit behind the debt is the customer's, which is why pricing on a neocloud's delayed-draw term loan reflects the counterparty more than the borrower; the exposure is only as good as that counterparty.
terms.source: The filer's revenue and commitments notes as printed; this site's own reading rule

terms.popup: Contracted future revenue divided by gross debt. Undiscounted revenue over multi-year terms against borrowings; above 1 is collateral, not cover, and it is only as good as the counterparty.
terms.definition: RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation (or LessorOperatingLeasePaymentsToBeReceived for a landlord) ÷ gross debt. The ratio the project lenders underwrite for a neocloud; read it with the counterparty's name and rating rather than as a coverage multiple.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy elements RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation and LessorOperatingLeasePaymentsToBeReceived; this site's own ratio

terms.popup: Debt raised by a subsidiary that holds the financed assets and contracts, where lenders can look only to those assets. A bankruptcy-remote entity is not automatically non-recourse; the collateral sentence says how far.
terms.definition: The borrowing entity and the recourse sentence as printed in the debt note. Non-recourse debt protects the parent's balance sheet, but some special-purpose subsidiaries' creditors keep recourse to the parent's assets, so the panel quotes the filing's own words per facility. BDCs use the same structure for their SPV financing facilities.
terms.source: The filer's debt note as printed; BXSL 10-Q 2026-06-30 for the BDC-side SPV facilities
terms.whereUsed: Deal ledger; debt panel; BDC liability ladder

terms.popup: A data-center campus owned mostly by a fund, with the hyperscaler as minority owner and tenant. The capex moves off the hyperscaler's balance sheet into a bond the fund's vehicle sells; the tenant's exposure is a lease plus a guarantee.
terms.definition: Development cost, ownership split, partner cash, lease commitment and residual value guarantee as printed in the filing. Unconsolidated, so the hyperscaler's exposure appears in commitments and guarantees, not in gross debt; the ledger records the structure once, with the URL, and the private-credit share counts the fund-partnered rows.
terms.source: The filer's commitments, guarantees and leases notes as printed; this site's own ledger method
terms.whereUsed: Deal ledger; sources and uses (partner funding)

terms.popup: The tenant's promise to make the owner whole if the asset is worth less than a set amount at the end of the lease. No liability is recorded, but it is the credit term that makes a campus bond investment grade.
terms.definition: Threshold and maximum exposure as printed in the leases or commitments note. Rating agencies treat it as contingent, debt-like exposure, which is why the hyperscaler's economic exposure to a joint-venture campus exceeds its lease payments; the panel shows the maximum exposure beside the lease with the note reference.
terms.source: ASC 842 lessee disclosures of residual value guarantees; the filer's leases or commitments note as printed

terms.popup: A guarantee by a hyperscaler of a tenant's lease payments to a developer. The credit behind the developer's bonds is the guarantor, not the tenant, so the guarantor's rating sizes the notes.
terms.definition: Recorded from the guarantee tags (GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure) and the filing's own description. On a default the guarantor may assume the lease rather than pay cash. Backstops are ledger rows with URLs and are excluded from every signed-financing total, since they are contingent.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure; the filer's guarantees note as printed

terms.popup: Preferred shares that convert into common stock at a set date within a price range. Equity for the rating agencies but with a fixed dividend: a way to raise equity-credit capital without a common-stock discount.
terms.definition: ProceedsFromIssuanceOfConvertiblePreferredStock where tagged; coupon, conversion range and settlement date as printed in the prospectus. Shown in the equity segment of sources and uses; the agency's equity-content treatment is quoted from its rating action, never assumed.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element ProceedsFromIssuanceOfConvertiblePreferredStock; the issuer's prospectus supplement as printed

terms.popup: Preferred units whose dividend accrues instead of being paid in cash, often with rate step-ups over time. Equity in form, debt in cost: the most expensive capital in the build-out ledger.
terms.definition: Rate, step-ups and any trigger terms as printed in the issuer's 8-K or note. Rating agencies may treat it as debt; a trigger that obliges the investor to add equity does not cut the accruing rate. It is the same PIK mechanism the BDC side reports as PIK income, seen from the issuer's side.
terms.source: The issuer's 8-K or note as printed; the same PIK mechanism as the BDC-side PIK entry

terms.popup: Cash received from customers before the capacity is delivered. A funding channel with no coupon, provided by the customer's own balance sheet, that sits inside operating cash flow and lowers capex-to-CFO.
terms.definition: IncreaseDecreaseInDeferredRevenue where tagged, Oracle's 'net cash outlay' reconciliation, or the filer's guidance sentence, each with its source. Because it is counted in operating cash flow, a build funded by prepayments looks self-funded on the capex-to-CFO ratio; the sources chart shows it as its own bar.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element IncreaseDecreaseInDeferredRevenue; Oracle's 8-K exhibit 99.1 reconciliation as printed
terms.whereUsed: Sources and uses; capex to operating cash flow caveat

terms.popup: What management said it would spend against what the cash-flow statement shows. A staircase that only rises is a company that kept underestimating; a definition change is labeled, never read as a cut.
terms.definition: Guidance as printed (a range, a run rate or a direction) against the outturn on the company's own metric and on the tagged line. The site never turns a run rate or a direction into a number; the error is computed only for numeric ranges on the same basis, and every row carries the transcript or filing URL.
terms.source: The company's guidance as printed in its earnings release or call transcript; this site's own comparison rule
terms.whereUsed: Guidance against outturn panel; chart H9

terms.popup: Oracle's own measure: capex minus customer prepayments and vendor financing tied to capex, from its earnings release table. Company-defined; the tagged cash-flow line is larger, and the gap is the customer- and vendor-funded slice.
terms.definition: capex − customer prepayments − short-term financing related to capex, as reconciled in Oracle's 8-K exhibit 99.1 table each quarter. The panel draws the tagged line and shows this measure beside it with the accession, never substituting one for the other; Oracle's guidance is on this basis.
terms.source: Oracle's 8-K exhibit 99.1 quarterly reconciliation table as printed

terms.popup: The yield premium over Treasuries at which a bond tranche priced, from its pricing term sheet. Not a secondary level and not an OAS, so it is drawn on its own axis beside the index, never subtracted from it.
terms.definition: Spread to the benchmark Treasury as printed on the FWP pricing term sheet for each tranche. Rising new-issue spreads for one issuer while the rating-band OAS is flat is issuer-specific repricing. For loans, LCD's new-issue direct-lending spreads are the analogue and join the spread ladder when the deck ingest lands.
terms.source: The issuer's FWP pricing term sheet as printed (SEC EDGAR form type FWP); LCD's new-issue direct-lending spreads for loans
terms.whereUsed: Ratings and spread context panel; M1 reference dot

terms.popup: An agency's assignment, affirmation, outlook change or move of a rating. On this site it is always a row with a date, agency and trigger sentence, never a number, and press-dated rows are drawn hollow.
terms.definition: Date, agency, rating, outlook, trigger sentence and source type per row. Moody's and Fitch pages sit behind logins, so their rows carry the press date and are drawn hollow; S&P's text is archived because its pages answer 403 to fetchers. Nothing is averaged across agencies.
terms.source: Moody's, S&P Global Ratings and Fitch press releases as dated; this site's own recording rule

terms.popup: Cash available for debt service divided by scheduled principal and interest. The covenant project lenders test on a delayed-draw facility. Definitions differ per facility, so the site prints the printed figure and never computes one.
terms.definition: As stated in the facility covenant or in the agency's base case. Each facility defines cash available for debt service its own way, so the ratio is disclosed-only: the filer's or agency's printed value with its source, by the site's own rule.
terms.source: The facility covenant or the rating agency's base case as printed; standard project-finance definition
terms.whereUsed: Neocloud leverage panel; deal ledger facility rows

terms.popup: Equipment bought on deferred payment terms from the supplier: a balance in the debt note, not a flow in the issuance tags. A fourth channel beside delayed-draw loans, notes and converts.
terms.definition: The filer's 'OEM and Software License Financing Arrangements' or similar line in its debt note, with balance and effective rate as printed. It is shown as a balance at period end with the accession; because it never passes through the debt-issuance tags it would otherwise vanish from a sources chart.
terms.source: The filer's debt note as printed (for example an 'OEM and Software License Financing Arrangements' line)

terms.popup: The portion of signed build-out financing provided by non-bank funds: private credit facilities plus fund-partnered joint ventures, divided by all signed rows. Stated with and without press-sourced rows.
terms.definition: Σ private credit facility and fund-partnered JV or SPV rows ÷ Σ signed rows in the deal ledger. Press-sourced rows carry a caveat marker and the share is stated both ways; a bank syndicate with undisclosed distribution stays 'bank loan'. It ties the build-out monitor to the Market view's private-credit growth charts by direction, not level.
terms.source: This site's own deal-ledger method
terms.whereUsed: Deal ledger summary; ties to the Market view

terms.popup: How June and May filers are placed beside December filers: each column is the calendar quarter containing the period end. Read a stacked quarter as 'the quarter each company's period ended in', never as a common ninety days.
terms.definition: column = the calendar quarter containing the period end; Oracle and Applied Digital (May year ends) sit one month early and are footnoted; a fiscal year that closes in the first half of the calendar year is named for the calendar year it began in, so Microsoft's and Oracle's FY2026 land in the 2025 row of aligned-year charts, with the filer's own label on hover.
terms.source: This site's own alignment rule
terms.fixNote: PR B: definition edited (column = the calendar quarter containing...)

terms.popup: Contracted revenue not yet recognized: the backlog a company has signed but not delivered. Undiscounted and spread over multi-year terms; the numerator of backlog to debt.
terms.definition: RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation, tagged by most filers with the share expected within twelve months. It is revenue, not cash, and is only as good as the counterparty, so the panel names the largest customers where the filing does.
terms.source: us-gaap taxonomy element RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation (ASC 606-10-50-13); each filer's revenue note
terms.whereUsed: Neocloud leverage panel; backlog to debt

terms.popup: A specialist provider that rents GPU compute to hyperscalers and model developers, building data centers on borrowed money against signed contracts. The section-15 cohort of six, each with its own filing basis.
terms.definition: The site's label for the six smaller listed compute providers in the build-out monitor, whose financing runs through delayed-draw term loans, SPV notes, converts and vendor financing rather than a hyperscaler's cash flow. Their SIC codes (6199 and blank) do not describe them, so the industry map carries an owner-set override; several file untagged 6-K statements, which the interim parser reads with hand-keyed accessions.
terms.source: This site's own label; the filers' SIC codes on the SEC submissions index

terms.popup: A bond sold directly to a small group of institutional investors, often insurers, without a public registration. A financing channel in the build-out ledger beside bank loans, public notes and private credit facilities.
terms.definition: Recorded as its own channel in the deal ledger with the filing or press URL; a private placement to insurers is not a private credit fund facility and is not counted in the private-credit share unless the filing names a fund as the lender.
terms.source: This site's own deal-ledger channel; the filing or press release as printed per row
